name: manual_8aa89c
claim: Reconciliation decisions (which side of a conflict, divergence, or finding is correct) should be made from what's actually verified to be there, not from which side looks more current by a fast heuristic (recency, version number, 'the other side is usually just behind'). The heuristic and the verified answer usually agree, which is exactly what makes skipping verification feel safe -- the cases where they diverge are silent regressions with no error message anywhere to catch them later.

decisions.notes: Capstone lesson from the 2026-08-09 CodeRabbit-remediation + branch-reanchor arc (see CODERABBIT_REMEDIATION_AND_REANCHOR_ARC_2026-08-09.md for the full narrative): this exact pattern recurred independently across 5 different domains in one session -- stale-branch-vs-main content (patch-id verified), security redaction vs a stale real LAN IP (redaction always wins regardless of recency), a CodeRabbit style-rule transfer across languages (researched bash idiom rather than assumed), a submodule gitlink pointer (verified direction, branch's pin turned out OLDER not newer), and a cross-repo guard-sync divergence question (ran the checker instead of trusting confident reasoning). Only the submodule case would have actually regressed if resolved by heuristic alone -- the other four happened to agree with 'take the newer-looking side,' which is precisely why the discipline of checking anyway, every time, is the actual lesson, not the individual outcomes.
